content.value_statement: Incident teams need clear steps before outages happen. This skill provides structured runbook templates for triage, mitigation, recovery, escalation, and updates.
actual_capabilities: Creates service outage runbooks with impact assessment, alerts, triage, mitigation, rollback, and verification sections.
Provides database incident procedures for connection exhaustion, replication lag, disk pressure, and recovery checks.
Includes escalation matrices for engineering, security, finance, legal, support, and incident command roles.
Drafts internal incident notifications, status updates, and resolution messages for stakeholders.
Organizes severity levels, response times, dashboards, and alert links into repeatable runbook formats.
limitations: It provides templates and examples, not automated incident detection or live monitoring.
Commands must be reviewed and adapted before use in any production environment.
It does not validate access permissions, service names, dashboards, or escalation contacts.
It cannot replace organization-specific incident policy, compliance review, or postmortem practice.

use_cases.title: Service Outage Preparation
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable outage runbook for a production service before the next on-call rotation.

use_cases.title: Database Incident Response
use_cases.description: Draft a database runbook covering connection pressure, replication lag, disk space, rollback, and verification.

use_cases.title: Incident Communication Standardization
use_cases.description: Prepare consistent internal updates, escalation paths, and resolution messages for high-severity incidents.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the incident-runbook-templates skill to create a SEV2 runbook for [service]. Include impact, alerts, first triage, mitigation, rollback, verification, escalation, and communication sections.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt a Database Runbook
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a database incident runbook for [database]. Cover connection pool exhaustion, replication lag, disk pressure, safe rollback, validation checks, and escalation contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Build Active Incident Steps
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft an active incident runbook for [current symptoms]. Separate diagnostic steps from mitigation steps. Mark any production-changing action for human approval before execution.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize a Runbook Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a runbook template library for [organization]. Include severity definitions, required sections, owner metadata, review cadence, escalation matrices, and communication templates.

output_examples.input: Create an outage runbook for a payment service.
output: A structured runbook with service ownership, impact assessment, alerts, triage, mitigation paths, rollback steps, verification checks, and communication templates.
A severity-based escalation matrix for engineering, security, finance, legal, and support stakeholders.

output_examples.input: Prepare a database incident runbook for replication lag.
output: A database-focused procedure covering lag assessment, replica health checks, failover considerations, recovery validation, and escalation timing.
A checklist that separates diagnostic checks from production-changing actions.

output_examples.input: Standardize incident updates for on-call teams.
output: Internal notification, status update, and resolution message templates with fields for severity, impact, owner, actions, and next update time.
Guidance for keeping stakeholders informed during investigation, mitigation, and recovery.

best_practices: Replace sample service names, endpoints, dashboards, and contacts with approved internal references.
Mark any rollback, scaling, database, or network action for review before execution.
Review each runbook after incidents and test it during scheduled readiness exercises.
anti_patterns: Do not paste example commands into production without environment-specific review.
Do not omit verification, rollback, or escalation sections from high-severity runbooks.
Do not rely on one person for incident decisions when escalation criteria are met.

faq.question: Does this skill execute incident response commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides runbook templates and example procedures that operators must review before use.

faq.question: Which incidents does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers service outages, degraded latency, partial failures, traffic surges, database pressure, replication lag, and disk pressure.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it include communication templates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes initial incident notices, status updates, resolution messages, and escalation matrix examples.

faq.question: Is it ready for regulated environments?
faq.answer: Not by itself. Legal, compliance, and security teams should review runbooks before regulated production use.

faq.question: How should teams maintain generated runbooks?
faq.answer: Teams should update runbooks after incidents, ownership changes, alert changes, and scheduled readiness tests.
